html:
Lesotho is a mountain kingdom in southern Africa, entirely surrounded by South Africa. It is the land of the Basotho people, and it exists because a king chose British protection over conquest by Boer settlers.

The kingdom was built in the 1820s by Moshoeshoe I. In the wars and upheaval of the Mfecane, he gathered refugees on Thaba Bosiu, a flat-topped mountain that enemies could not take. He held off rivals with diplomacy as much as war.

From the 1850s the Orange Free State fought him for the fertile farmland west of the Caledon River, and the Basotho lost much of it. In 1868 Moshoeshoe asked Britain for protection, and the country became Basutoland.

  • 1871 to 1884: run from the Cape Colony; a Basotho revolt, the Gun War of 1880 to 1881, ended that.
  • 1884: a crown colony ruled directly from London.
  • 1910: kept out of the Union of South Africa.
  • 1966: independence as the Kingdom of Lesotho.
  • 1970: the ruling party cancelled an election it had lost; army rule followed from 1986 to 1993.

With little farmland and few jobs, many Basotho men worked for generations in South Africa's mines, starting with the Witwatersrand gold fields. Today Lesotho also sells water from its highlands to South Africa through large dams and tunnels.
sum: Lesotho is a mountain kingdom in southern Africa, entirely surrounded by South Africa. It is the land of the Basotho people, and it exists because a king chose British protection over conquest by Boer settlers.
